extracted.intended_audience: Recording Academy members, artists, record labels, producers, engineers, music supervisors and other music industry professionals submitting recordings for GRAMMY consideration
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and screening criteria for GRAMMY Awards categories, plus definitions of eligible credits (producers, engineers, music supervisors), statuette/certificate/ticketing policies, and the proposals process for rule/category changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate eligibility for contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates may be issued to contributors such as Producer & Engineer with less than 50 percent playing time of newly recorded material; Mastering Engineer, if other than Artist; Lyricist(s) & Composer(s) if they have written/composed a score that comprises greater than 50 percent playing time of the album and has not been previously nominated; Engineer(s)/Mixer(s) of greater than 50 percent playing time on the album; up to four Principal Vocalist(s) with significant contributing performance(s) (defined as a lead performance by a featured vocalist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates are issued for Vocalists in 'ensemble-driven pieces.' Use playing-time thresholds and the 'significant contributing performance' definition to determine certificate eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Artist / in-studio Producer award assignment for albums
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards go to Principal Artist(s) with significant contributing performances and/or in-studio Producer(s) of a majority of the tracks on the album. If those are absent, award to the individual(s) proactively responsible for the concept and musical direction of the album and for the selection of artists, songs and producers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which individuals had majority responsibility for concept/musical direction and track production when assigning awards for an album.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different crediting for albums of pre-existing masters vs new recordings
rubrics_metrics.description: For albums consisting largely of pre-existing masters: up to two album Producers and up to two Music Supervisors (per criteria). For albums consisting largely of new recordings: awards to Principal Artist(s) with significant contributing performances (ensemble-driven casts with comparable participation are not eligible); up to three Producers (appeal for a fourth in extraordinary circumstances); and up to two Music Supervisors. Engineer/Mixer(s) of greater than 50 percent playing time of newly recorded material may also be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify the album as primarily pre-existing or new recordings to apply the correct limits and eligible roles; ensemble-driven casts are generally ineligible for principal-artist awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score Soundtrack (Film/TV) eligibility by playing time
rubrics_metrics.description: Composer, Producer & Engineer/Mixer of greater than 50 percent playing time on the album are eligible for awards in Score Soundtrack for Visual Media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the >50% playing-time threshold to composer/producer/engineer credits for awarding in score soundtrack categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score Soundtrack for Video Games — composer/producer/engineer thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Composer, Music Producer & Engineer/Mixer are eligible. When more than one composer is listed, a minimum of 33 percent playing time will be required. If a composer has a separate production team, the 33 percent applies to the Music Producer(s) and Engineer(s)/Mixer(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 33% minimum playing-time threshold when multiple composers or separate production teams are present; certificates to Composer/Producer/Engineer of less than 33% may be issued if other than artist.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Certificates Issued (certain package/notes/historical categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some categories (e.g., certain Package, Notes and Historical categories) explicitly note 'No Certificates Issued.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check category-specific language to confirm whether certificates are issued; do not assume certificate issuance unless specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designer/Illustrator/Photographer eligibility for package awards
rubrics_metrics.description: For Recording Package and Boxed or Special Limited-Edition Package categories, Designer, Illustrator & Photographer are eligible contributors if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate visual-arts credits for package-related categories when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Album Notes and Historical Album contributor eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Album Notes Writer is eligible for Album Notes; Compilation Producer, Restoration Engineer & Mastering Engineer are eligible for Historical Album.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical Album credits focus on restoration and compilation production; album-note awards go to the writer of the liner notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Songwriter Of The Year, Non-Classical eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Songwriter(s) must have a minimum of five newly written songs in which they are listed as a non-performing, non-producing songwriter or co-writer to be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count newly written songs where the songwriter is credited as non-performing/non-producing; certificates are not issued for this Category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineered Album eligibility (Non-Classical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineers (see P&E list for eligible credits) and Mastering Engineer are recognized in Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Producers & Engineers list for which engineer credits qualify for eligibility in engineered-album categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer Of The Year and Remixed Recording eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Producer(s) are eligible for Producer Of The Year; Remixer(s) are eligible for Remixed Recording. For Producer Of The Year/Remixed Recording, 'No Certificates Issued' may apply to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producer and remixer credits are category-specific; verify certificate policies per category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immersive Audio Album eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: IA Engineer, IA Producer & IA Mastering Engineer are eligible, and if an album is released only in multichannel format, Producer(s) and Engineer(s) receive an award. Producer & Engineer of greater than 50 percent of original recordings may be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify immersive-audio-specific credits and playing-time thresholds when determining award recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical category eligibility rules (conductors, soloists, producers, engineers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classical categories specify awards to roles such as Conductor, Orchestra/Large Ensemble; Producer & Engineer if other than Artist, of greater than 50 percent playing time; Principal Soloists; Composer(s) & Librettist for new complete-opera recordings (if they wrote 100% of music/libretto).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply role- and playing-time-based rules for each classical category; full authorship may be required for composer/librettist recognition in certain categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music Video and Music Film award credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Music Video awards go to Artist, Video Director & Video Producer. Music Film awards go to Artist, Video Director & Video Producer (of over 51 percent of the total playing time of the music video). Audio Producer, Audio Mixer & Video Editor may also be recognized depending on conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the >51% playing-time threshold for music-film director/producer eligibility; other technical/video credits may be eligible per category language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of Award — terms and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of any award is deemed to constitute acceptance by the recipient (and successors) of all Recording Academy terms and conditions under which the award was given, including Board-approved rules/policies. Recipients must acknowledge and agree in writing to such terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should be aware that acceptance binds them to Academy policies and may require written acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statuette possession and commercial use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Possession of a GRAMMY statuette is granted on the condition it will not be used other than for the recipient’s personal, non-commercial purposes. Sale, auction, public exhibition, reproduction, or other commercial exploitation without express prior written consent of the Recording Academy is prohibited and may result in repossession of the statuette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients (and any transferees) are bound by these restrictions; unauthorized transfer does not convey rights and may trigger repossession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Academy ownership/reservation of rights in awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules may state particular awards or categories shall be the property of, and all rights therein reserved by, the Recording Academy (except the right of possession), and awards shall not be sold, transferred or assigned by the recipient without express written consent of the Recording Academy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must secure written consent before any transfer of rights; property/rights language can vary by award/category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of GRAMMY statuettes for groups and ensembles
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals and eligible members of groups of nine or fewer who are GRAMMY nominees on a winning project receive a GRAMMY statuette. Groups of 10 or more members receive one statuette for the entire group/ensemble (individual members are not GRAMMY winners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the group-size thresholds (<=9, 10–20, >20) to determine individual statuette eligibility and alternative recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large group pins, certificates and ticketing
rubrics_metrics.description: For large groups between 10 and 20 members, the Academy provides a special certificate and pin to each member; certificates indicate members are part of a large group on a nominated recording. For these groups, GRAMMY tickets are made available to group members even though they are not nominees. For groups with more than 20 members, only the group leader is designated as a nominee and no pins, certificates, tickets, or statuettes are available to the group members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 10–20 and >20 member rules to determine provision of pins, certificates and ticketing availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Album Of The Year ticketing allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: For Album Of The Year nominees, telecast and related event tickets go to Artist(s) and Featured Artist(s), Songwriter(s) of new material, Producer(s), Recording Engineer(s), Mixer(s), and Mastering Engineer(s) credited with at least 33 percent playing time of the album, if other than the Artist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the 33% playing-time threshold to non-artist contributors when allocating tickets for Album Of The Year nominees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards & Nominations proposals process and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Members may submit proposals for changes to rules, guidelines, definitions year-round; cutoff for proposals to be considered for the following year is March 1. New Category proposals require a special submission form and require a two-thirds supermajority vote of both the Awards & Nominations Committee and the Board of Trustees to pass. Proposals that pass Trustees go into effect immediately for the next GRAMMY Awards; proposals rejected by the Committee are not considered again the next consecutive year except under limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow submission deadlines and form requirements; expect committee debate/vote and possible Trustee ratification; resubmission is restricted and requires significant justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer & Engineer eligibility compilation and >50% rule for genre albums
rubrics_metrics.description: The Producers & Engineers Wing maintains credits/definitions for determining eligibility. Producers and engineers receive GRAMMY statuettes in any Category where they are eligible to be nominated. Additionally, for genre album Categories (e.g., Best Country Album), eligible producers and engineers who have worked on greater than 50 percent of the playing time of a winning album receive a GRAMMY statuette (these contributors are compiled and audited after the telecast and are not nominees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Wing's credit definitions and the >50% playing-time rule to determine statuette recipients in genre album categories; verification/audit occurs post-telecast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and duties of Producer (eligible credit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Producer is the primary person(s) contracted by and accountable to the content owner for delivering the recording as a finished product. Duties include: overseeing recording sessions; making creative, technical and aesthetic decisions; choosing final takes; participating in song selection; overseeing selection of personnel and supplying accurate credit information; overseeing staffing, budgets, schedules, mixing, mastering and quality control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this duties list to evaluate whether a credited producer performed sufficient responsibilities to be eligible as a Producer for GRAMMY recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-Producer definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-Producer generally shares some or all of the Producer’s responsibilities with a Producer or another Co-Producer and is assigned a co-producer credit by the artist/content owner. A Co-Producer makes significant and consequential contributions to the production outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-Producer credits should reflect significant contributions; assignment is determined by artist/content owner and reviewed for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocal Producer / 'Vocals Produced By' credit
rubrics_metrics.description: This person has overall creative and technical control of the vocal recording on a project and the individual recording sessions involved; they work directly with vocalists and engineers and make creative/aesthetic decisions realizing the goals of artist and label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vocal producers must be present for vocal sessions and exercise creative control to be eligible for vocal-production credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compilation Producer eligibility (limited categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compilation Producer credit is eligible only in Best Compilation Soundtrack For Visual Media and Best Historical Album Categories; this person supervises and/or exercises control over work assigned to other producers/engineers and has primary creative responsibility for selection of tracks and components on a compilation or historical album.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this limited-eligibility definition when evaluating compilation soundtrack or historical album credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immersive Audio Producer equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Immersive Audio Producer has the same responsibilities as a Producer, but specifically for an immersive audio recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the Producer duties to immersive audio context when assessing eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-eligible producer credits (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-eligible producer credits include Executive Producer (often a label rep or funder), Assistant/Associate/Additional Producer (delegated responsibilities reporting to Producer), 'Strings (or Any Other Instrument) Produced By' (works on an element not overall production), and 'Produced on Behalf of (the Content Owner)' (acts more like executive/A&R rather than day-to-day production).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credits that denote executive, partial, or delegated roles are not generally eligible as primary Producer credits for GRAMMY statuettes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and duties of Engineer (eligible credits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineer is the primary person(s) actively responsible for the creative process of recording and/or mixing and technical decisions. Responsibilities include operating/overseeing recording equipment, making creative technical/aesthetic choices in collaboration with artist/producer, and realizing the sounds/concepts for the project. Specific eligible credits include Recording Engineer/Recorded By, Mixed By/Mixer/Mix Engineer, Remix Engineer (Best Remixed Recording only), Vocals Recorded/Engineered By, Balance Engineer (Classical), Mastering Engineer (eligible in specified categories), Tonmeister (Classical with specific qualifications), Restoration Engineer (Best Historical Album), and Immersive Audio Engineer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether engineers made creative and technical decisions beyond mere operation; certain specialized roles (e.g., mastering, restoration) have category-specific eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastering engineer eligibility exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastering engineers are eligible to receive a GRAMMY statuette only in the Categories of Best Historical Album; Best Immersive Audio Album; Best Engineered Album, Classical; Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical; Record Of The Year; and Album Of The Year. Mastering engineers are eligible to receive a Winner’s Certificate for all winning genre albums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume mastering engineers get statuettes in all categories; consult the list of categories where they are statuette-eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tonmeister qualification (Classical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tonmeister performs the same work as an engineer or balance engineer, but to use the title correctly they must be a graduate of an official Tonmeister program that includes score reading, electronics training and education in recording, mixing and editing techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify Tonmeister educational credentials when the credit is used for classical-engineering eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration Engineer role (Historical Album)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration Engineer transfers and repairs original flat source tapes and discs, removes or reduces anomalies/unwanted noise, and prepares flawed/compromised recordings for the mastering engineer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration engineers are eligible specifically for Best Historical Album; assess their technical restoration contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-eligible engineer credits (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-eligible engineering credits include Pro Tools Engineer/Operator, Pro Tools Editor, Additional Pro Tools Engineer, Engineer for Mix (assistant to mixer), Assistant Engineer/Second Engineer, Additional Engineer (small percentage of project), Assistant Mix Engineer/Mix Assistant, Mix Programming, Digital Editing, Digital Engineering/Programming, and DSD Recording roles—generally roles focused on technical operation/maintenance or minor contributions not making major aesthetic judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credits that are operational, archival, or denote limited/assisting contributions are ordinarily not eligible for GRAMMY statuettes as primary engineer credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music Supervisor responsibilities and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Music Supervisor must identify, secure and supervise all music-related talent; possess accurate knowledge of costs; determine and advise on financial needs and generate realistic budgets; advise on schedule feasibility; deliver music elements to technical requirements; manage and secure legal rights (synchronization and master use licenses, clearances, credits, cue sheets); and determine viability/creation/securing of ancillary products (soundtracks, singles, videos, downloads) for promotion/revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Music Supervisors are credited for coordinating creative, legal, budgetary and delivery aspects; eligibility for awards depends on category-specific language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Of The Year screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings entered should represent the best overall achievement. Elements to be considered are the performance, production and engineering; secondary elements are songwriting/composition, arranging and performance of backup vocalists and musicians, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening should weight performance, production and engineering most heavily; songwriting/arranging are secondary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Album Of The Year screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Albums entered should represent the best overall achievement by the performer(s), album producer(s), engineer(s)/mixer(s), and songwriter(s). Other elements to be considered are arranging and musicianship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the collective achievement across performance, production, engineering and songwriting when screening albums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Song Of The Year screening criteria and songwriting eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Songs entered should represent the best achievement in songwriting. A song must comprise melody and lyrics to be eligible in a songwriting Category and must have been released on a recording for the first time, or achieved prominence for the first time, during the current eligibility year. Songs that contain samples or interpolations are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only consider songwriting merits (melody and lyrics); verify first release or first prominence within eligibility year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best New Artist screening criteria and eligibility limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: This Category recognizes an artist whose eligibility-year release(s) achieved a breakthrough into public consciousness and notably impacted the musical landscape. Primary element is the artist’s performance. Minimum releases to meet eligibility: five singles/tracks or one album. There is no specified maximum number of releases, but Screening Committees determine whether the artist had attained breakthrough or prominence prior to the eligibility year; prior breakthrough or prior GRAMMY nomination as a performer makes an artist ineligible (with specific exceptions). An artist may not enter this Category more than three times (including as a performing member of an established group). Eligible and Not Eligible lists define boundaries (e.g., solo artists, established duos/groups are eligible; choir/large ensembles, non-music-performing video performers, musical craftspeople are not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate breakthrough status primarily by performance and audience impact; apply minimum-release rule and check past nominations/performances to determine eligibility; consult exceptions carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Pop Solo Performance screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in a solo vocal or instrumental pop performance with or without accompaniment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen for artistic excellence in pop performance irrespective of accompaniment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Pop Duo/Group Performance screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in a duo, group or collaborative vocal or instrumental pop performance. Recordings on which a group receives artist billing are eligible even when the vocal features only one member. The entire group or collaborative performance, rather than presence of a lead vocal, determines eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the collective group/collaborative performance when determining eligibility for duo/group categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For vocal-only albums of a type/style that cannot be intermingled with present forms of pop music (e.g., Great American Songbook, cabaret/musical theater-style songs, traditional pop style). Includes contemporary pop songs performed in a traditional pop style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen for stylistic characteristics of 'traditional' pop; consider composition, vocal styling and instrumental arrangement rather than age of material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Pop Vocal Album screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes artistic excellence in pop vocal albums (vocal only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate overall vocal artistry and album concept within pop genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Dance/Electronic Recording screening criteria and new-material rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended for recordings with significant electronic-based instrumentation generally based around a rhythmic dance beat. Screening should include established and emerging dance/electronic genres. Category is open to recordings targeted to the dance/electronic market. Dance remixes are eligible only in Best Remixed Recording and may not be entered in Best Dance/Electronic Recording. Recording MUST contain greater than 50 percent new material; if vocals or any significant part of the music have not been recorded within the last five years or were released prior to the year’s eligibility period, it can only be entered in Best Remixed Recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure recordings are >50% new material and appropriately electronic/dance in instrumentation/beat; remixes belong in Remixed Recording category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Dance/Electronic Music Album screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in dance/electronic music albums with significant electronic-based instrumentation and a rhythmic dance beat. Albums of remixes are not eligible; remixes may be entered in Best Remixed Recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess album-level consistency in dance/electronic style; exclude albums that are solely remixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Contemporary Instrumental Album screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemporary instrumental music embraces a variety of musical genres. The album concept and production should emphasize instrumental performance, arrangement and/or melodic content and contain contemporary stylistic elements setting it apart from well-established instrumental styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen for album concept/production that foregrounds instrumental performance and contemporary stylistic elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Rock/Metal Performance and Best Rock Album screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Rock Performance recognizes artistic excellence in a rock performance by solo artists, collaborating artists, duos, or groups. Best Metal Performance recognizes excellence in a metal performance similarly. Best Rock Album recognizes artistic excellence in albums across the rock spectrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate performances/albums for artistic excellence within rock/metal idioms across subgenres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Rock Song (songwriting) screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A songwriter’s award recognizing the best achievement in songwriting across rock music, including metal. Only the merits of the song itself are considered. Songs with samples or interpolations are eligible. A song must comprise melody and lyrics and must have been released for the first time or achieved prominence during the eligibility year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess songwriting merits (structure, melody, lyrics); verify first release/prominence in eligibility period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Field screening criteria (Performance and Album)
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Alternative Music Performance recognizes artistic excellence in alternative performances that embrace progression and innovation in music and attitude, often more original/eclectic/musically challenging. Best Alternative Music Album recognizes artistic excellence in alternative albums and may include recordings that do not fit other genre categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen for progression, innovation, originality and eclecticism when evaluating alternative music.

rubrics_metrics.name: R&B Field screening criteria (performance, songwriting, progressive album)
rubrics_metrics.description: Best R&B Performance recognizes excellence in an R&B performance. Best Traditional R&B Performance recognizes excellence in traditional R&B that may incorporate blues, gospel and jazz elements. Best R&B Song recognizes excellence in R&B songwriting reflecting the broad spectrum of R&B style and culture (songs with melody and lyrics released/first prominent in eligibility year are eligible). Best Progressive R&B Album recognizes excellence in albums of progressive vocal tracks derivative of R&B and may incorporate samples/elements of hip-hop, rap, dance and electronic music and production elements from multiple genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider stylistic intention, song structure, lyrical content and musical presentation relative to R&B traditions and progressive innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rap Field screening criteria and Best Melodic Rap Performance specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Rap Performance recognizes excellence in rap performance (vocal only). Best Melodic Rap Performance recognizes excellence in performances that use delivery of rap and melody over modern production; requires a strong and clear presence of melody combined with rap cadence and is inclusive of dialects/lyrics/performance elements from non-rap genres. Both the song and melody should fit these criteria to be accepted in the Category. Best Rap Song recognizes excellence in rap songwriting; Best Rap Album recognizes album-level excellence (vocal performances only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For melodic rap, verify both rap cadence and a clear melodic presence; for rap songwriting, assess songwriting merits and confirm first release/prominence within eligibility period.
